text:
I was in my third year of medical school when this happened. I'm writing it in detail because I've had to tell it so many times, to police, to the university, to my therapist, that it has become a kind of script, but I'll try to write what it felt like rather than just what happened.

There was a party in a flat on the third floor of an old building. I'd taken LSD a handful of times before, always in calm settings. That night a friend of mine, I'll call him M, had brought some tabs, and five or six of us took one each around 10pm. M took two. The flat had a small balcony overlooking a courtyard, with a low iron railing.

For the first two hours it was a great party. Music, dancing, a lot of laughing. I remember lying on the floor watching the ceiling lamp turn into a jellyfish and thinking how lucky I was to have these friends. M was in a very euphoric mood, talking about how he felt he could fly, but we all laughed because he always said stuff like that.

Around midnight, I went out onto the balcony to get some air. M was there, sitting on the railing with his legs dangling over the courtyard, looking at the sky. I said something like 'mate, get down from there'. He laughed and said he wanted to touch the moon. I remember the moon looked enormous, like it was right above us, and in my state it seemed almost reasonable that he'd want to touch it. I don't know why I didn't grab him immediately. I've asked myself that question a thousand times.

He stood up on the railing. I reached out for him and my hand touched his jacket, and then he wasn't there. There was no scream. Just a silence, and then a sound from the courtyard below, a sound I will never be able to describe and never forget.

I looked over the railing. He was lying on the cobblestones, twisted, not moving. On LSD, the courtyard was swirling, the cobblestones were moving like water, and his body looked like it was sinking into them. I screamed. People came running onto the balcony. Someone started screaming too. Someone else called an ambulance. I ran down the stairs, three floors, I don't remember the stairs at all, and I was in the courtyard next to him.

And here is the thing that haunts me most. I'm a medical student. I knew what to do, in theory. Check airway, breathing, circulation. Don't move his neck. But I couldn't think. My hands were shaking and they kept changing shape. His face was bleeding and the blood was a colour I'd never seen, too bright, glowing. I could hear him breathing, a horrible gurgling sound, and I didn't know if I was hearing it or imagining it. I knelt next to him and held his hand and said his name over and over. A neighbour came out, an older man, and he was the one who actually did something useful: he kept M's head still and talked to the ambulance dispatcher. I just knelt there.

The ambulance and the police arrived together. The lights. Blue lights bouncing off the walls of the courtyard, turning everything into a strobe nightmare. The paramedics pushed me away, which was right. I watched them work on him. They put a collar on him and a mask and lifted him onto a stretcher. One of them asked me what he'd taken and I said LSD, and he looked at my eyes and said 'and you too, I see'.

The police separated everyone and took our names. A young officer asked me to describe what happened. I tried. I said he wanted to touch the moon. She wrote that down with a blank face. I realised how insane it sounded. I started to believe that they'd think I pushed him. My hand had been on his jacket. Had I pushed him? In that state I genuinely didn't know. Maybe I had. Maybe I'd reached out to grab him and actually pushed. I've had that doubt ever since, even though I know rationally that I didn't.

They let us go around 3am. I didn't know if M was alive. I walked home alone through the city, still tripping. Every streetlight looked like the moon. Every sound was that sound from the courtyard. When I got home I sat in the shower with my clothes on and stayed there until the water ran cold, and then I stayed there anyway.

At 7am, a friend texted that M was alive, in intensive care, with a broken pelvis, broken arm and a head injury. He survived. He's mostly recovered now, with some lasting problems with his leg. He doesn't remember anything from that night after about 11pm.

Wir waren zu dritt in einer Hütte im Schwarzwald und hatten Pilze gegessen. Gegen Abend ist der Strom ausgefallen, wahrscheinlich wegen eines Sturms. Wir hatten nur ein paar Kerzen. In dem flackernden Licht wurde die Hütte zu einem fremden, bedrohlichen Ort. Die Schatten an den Wänden haben sich bewegt und Gestalten gebildet. Ich hörte draußen Schritte, ganz deutlich, rund um die Hütte. Die anderen sagten, das sei der Wind, aber ich war mir sicher, dass jemand da draußen ist und uns beobachtet.

Dann ist einer meiner Freunde rausgegangen, um nach dem Sicherungskasten zu sehen, und kam nicht zurück. Fünf Minuten, zehn Minuten, zwanzig Minuten. Für mich war es eine Ewigkeit. Ich war mir sicher, dass ihn das Wesen draußen geholt hat und dass wir die Nächsten sind. Ich habe mich mit dem anderen Freund in eine Ecke gesetzt, wir haben uns aneinander geklammert. Ich habe gezittert und konnte nicht mehr klar denken. Ich habe angefangen zu beten, obwohl ich nicht gläubig bin.

Als er schließlich zurückkam, nass und lachend, weil er sich im Dunkeln verlaufen hatte, habe ich ihn angeschrien und dann geweint. Er hat nicht verstanden, warum ich so reagiere. Der Strom kam die ganze Nacht nicht zurück, und ich habe bis zum Morgengrauen mit offenen Augen dagesessen und auf die Tür gestarrt.

I took a small dose of mushrooms on a day off and then got an unexpected call for a video job interview an hour later. I said yes because I needed the job. I logged on and the interviewer's face was melting on the screen. I couldn't follow the questions. I could see my own face in the corner and it looked like a stranger. I panicked and ended the call saying my internet was down. Then I spent hours terrified that they'd somehow know and that I'd ruined my career.

I went to a retreat in Mexico for a week of ayahuasca ceremonies. The ceremonies were held in an open-sided palapa in the jungle. On the third night, at the peak of a very strong experience, I felt a sudden burning pain in my foot, like being stabbed with a hot needle. I looked down and in the candlelight I saw a scorpion crawling away.

The pain spread up my leg. My foot went numb and then my lips started tingling. In my state I was convinced that I was dying, that the poison was moving towards my heart and that I had maybe minutes left. The visions turned into scorpions, thousands of them pouring out of the ground and over my body. I screamed. One of the facilitators came over, and when I told her, she looked at my foot and said it was probably a scorpion and that most of them in the area weren't dangerous to adults. But she also looked worried and went to get the retreat leader.

They decided to take me to a local clinic, which was 40 minutes away on a bumpy dirt road. I lay in the back of a pickup truck, still in the middle of the ayahuasca, vomiting over the side, with my foot burning and the stars swirling overhead. I thought I was going to die in that truck. I said goodbye to my family in my head. I had visions of my mother crying at my funeral.

At the clinic the doctor gave me an injection and kept me under observation for the night. The sting turned out to be painful but not life-threatening. I lay on a hard bed in a white room under a fluorescent light, alone, still feeling the effects of the brew. A gecko on the wall kept turning into a scorpion. I didn't sleep. The next morning I was driven back to the retreat, where everyone wanted to hear about my 'initiation'. I left two days early.

Ich hatte mit meinem Freund LSD genommen und dazu Wein getrunken. Wir haben angefangen, über unsere Beziehung zu reden, und das ist eskaliert. Mitten im Trip hat er Schluss gemacht und ist gegangen. Ich war allein, völlig aufgelöst, und hatte das Gefühl, dass die Welt zusammenbricht. Ich habe stundenlang auf dem Boden gelegen und geweint, und die Wände haben mich erdrückt.

I'd followed an online wellness influencer who sold a course about 'healing your inner child with a heroic dose'. The course said that 5g of dried mushrooms alone in silent darkness was the way to break through trauma. I followed the instructions exactly. I'd been bullied badly at school and I thought this would heal it.

What happened was that I relived the bullying. Not remembered, relived. I was 12 again in the school toilets, with the older boys holding my head down. I could smell the bleach, hear their laughter. Then it got worse, because the trip added things: the boys' faces became demonic, their laughter became a roar, and I was not just in the toilets but in some kind of hell made of toilets, endless rows, and every one had a boy laughing at me.

I tried to tell myself it was the mushrooms, but that thought kept slipping away. I became convinced I deserved all of it, that I was worthless and disgusting, that everyone who'd ever met me had secretly despised me. I curled up on the floor and hit myself in the face, which I hadn't done since school.

When it ended, eight hours later, I lay there exhausted with a bruised cheek. The course had a section called 'integration' which said to journal about your breakthrough. I didn't have a breakthrough. I had the worst night of my life.

Ich war mit zwei Freunden in Prag und wir hatten im Hostel Pilze genommen. Während wir unterwegs waren, wurde in unser Zimmer eingebrochen, und als wir zurückkamen, waren unsere Rucksäcke weg, mit Pässen und Laptops. Ich stand mitten im Trip in diesem verwüsteten Zimmer und hatte das Gefühl, dass die ganze Welt gegen uns ist. Die Rezeption hat die Polizei gerufen, und ich musste in einem kleinen Büro Fragen beantworten, während die Wände sich bewegt haben. Ich konnte kaum sprechen und hatte Angst, dass sie merken, dass wir Drogen genommen haben, und uns verhaften. Ich habe mich die ganze Zeit wie ein Verbrecher gefühlt, obwohl wir die Opfer waren.
Acid plus ketamine at a party. I couldn't feel my arms or legs and was sure I'd been paralysed for life.

I took LSD at a friend's house and around the peak my heart started racing at what felt like 200 beats a minute. I panicked and asked my friend to take me to A&E. In the hospital, while waiting, I tried to explain what I'd taken, but I was confused and kept laughing nervously, and the triage nurse wrote 'possible psychosis'. When I tried to leave because the waiting room was too bright and loud, two security guards stopped me. I struggled and they held my arms behind my back. A doctor came and I was given an injection without anyone explaining what it was. I woke up hours later on a trolley in a corridor with a cannula in my arm and no idea how much time had passed. The ECG showed sinus tachycardia, nothing dangerous. I was discharged in the morning with a leaflet about drug use. I felt like I'd been treated like a criminal.

Ich habe als Studentin bei einem Besuch in meinem Elternhaus mit meinem Bruder Pilze genommen, als unsere Eltern eigentlich übers Wochenende weg sein sollten. Mein Vater hat früher viel getrunken und war dann oft gewalttätig, vor allem gegenüber meiner Mutter. Inzwischen ist er trocken, aber die Erinnerungen sind geblieben.

Mitten im Trip hörten wir den Schlüssel in der Tür. Mein Vater kam früher zurück, allein, weil er sich mit meiner Mutter gestritten hatte. Er war nicht betrunken, aber er war wütend und laut. In dem Moment, als ich seine Stimme im Flur hörte, war ich wieder acht Jahre alt. Ich habe mich in meinem alten Kinderzimmer unter der Bettdecke versteckt, genau wie damals. Ich hörte durch die Wand das Geschrei von früher, das Klirren von Gläsern, meine Mutter, die weint. Ich wusste nicht mehr, was jetzt passiert und was damals passiert ist.

Mein Bruder hat versucht, mit meinem Vater zu reden und ihn abzulenken, aber auch er war völlig verwirrt. Ich habe stundenlang unter der Decke gelegen und mich nicht bewegt, aus Angst, dass er reinkommt. Ich hatte das Gefühl, mein ganzes erwachsenes Leben sei nur ein Traum gewesen und ich sei immer noch das kleine Mädchen in diesem Haus. Als ich am nächsten Morgen aufgewacht bin, hat mein Vater Frühstück gemacht und so getan, als sei nichts gewesen. Für ihn war ja auch nichts gewesen.

I took part in a psilocybin trial for smoking cessation. The session was challenging. For about two hours I felt like I was dying of lung cancer, I could feel my lungs filling with tar, and I saw my own funeral. The therapists stayed with me. It was terrifying but it also made the risk very real.
LSD. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass mein Herz stehen bleibt, und habe stundenlang meinen Puls gemessen.
